brief:
Gasoline prices in Israel will reach an all-time high in early September, according to Shehab Wire. The fuel will cost 8.25 shekels—approximately $2.77—per liter, marking the highest price ever recorded in the country. The Ministry of Energy and Infrastructure approved the increase.

The new rate continues a steep climb in fuel costs that has weighed on Israeli consumers and businesses in recent months. The spike reflects broader pressures on global energy markets and domestic pricing policies.
